Every bacterium is a prokaryote..why: Stated explicitly and often ('bacteria are prokaryotes' 925, 'bacteria are prokaryotic' 411) and in the lead of Wikipedia's Bacteria article. It is close to definitional, so a model holds it directly.

sources.quote: They constitute a large domain of prokaryotic microorganisms.

Every virus is made of cells..why: False: a virus is not a cell. It replicates only inside the cells of a host, and its particles are genetic material in a protein coat.

sources.quote: A virus is a submicroscopic infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.

viruses exist in the form of independent viral particles, or virions, consisting of (i) genetic material, i.e., long molecules of DNA or RNA that encode the structure of the proteins by which the virus acts; (ii) a protein coat

notes: TBox revision. The rule is close to the definition of the domain (every bacterium is a prokaryote) and held by every model. The three derived queries name real bacteria that a model knows at most as bacteria, and state that membership in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops); the third is an application (a database field), whose two allowed values are named in the prompt as in the direct question, so this record has a 50% floor throughout (the relation has two values). Thermus aquaticus was dropped (Claude review flag: it is well known through Taq polymerase, so its cell type may be stored by name). The three now used are named a prokaryote in Dolma at most 7 times each. The earlier background-belief queries on E. coli and blue-green algae are gone (TBox records are determinate only); the blue-green algae check that three models missed went with them. The Chinese question was rephrased (属于 ... 还是 ...) after two models missed the earlier wording while holding the fact in English; it still needs a re-audit. The negation is asked as "Is it true that bacteria are not eukaryotes?" instead of "Is it false that ...?". Conjunction side fact: fungi are eukaryotes (true); disjunction side fact: every virus is made of cells (false). Near unrelated: the name for a rod-shaped bacterium (a bacillus), a class-level fact about bacteria untouched by the edit; its reference differs from the new answer. Paired with contraction biology-delete-0008 and the TBox expansion paired with this record.
